why_it_matters.text: The veto is the President's biggest tool to push back on Congress. When the President disagrees with a bill, a veto can stop it from becoming law. But the system has a check on the check: Congress can override a veto with a two-thirds vote in both chambers.

fun_fact.text: Presidents use the veto very differently. Franklin D. Roosevelt vetoed 635 bills — the all-time record. George Washington vetoed just 2 in his entire 8 years. Congress can override a veto with a two-thirds vote in both chambers, but it's so hard that only about 4% of all vetoes have ever been overturned.
